items.stem: What is the difference between weather and climate?

options.text: Weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere; climate is the long-term average over many years
options.rationale: Correct: climate is the long-term pattern, weather is short-term.

options.text: They mean exactly the same thing
options.rationale: They are related but not the same.

options.text: Weather is the long-term average and climate is today's conditions
Climate only describes the weather on a single day
options.rationale: Climate spans many years, not one day.

items.explanation: Correct: climate is the long-term pattern, weather is short-term.

items.stem: How does the natural greenhouse effect keep Earth warm enough for life? (Select ONE)

options.text: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit heat, slowing its escape to space
options.rationale: Correct: greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat, warming the surface.

options.text: Greenhouse gases block all sunlight from reaching Earth
options.rationale: They mainly affect outgoing heat, not incoming light.

options.text: They cool the Earth by reflecting heat away
options.rationale: They trap heat rather than mainly cooling.

options.text: They create new energy inside the atmosphere
options.rationale: They redistribute heat; they do not create energy.

items.explanation: Correct: greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat, warming the surface.

items.stem: Select TWO human activities that add extra greenhouse gases to the atmosphere. (Select TWO)

options.text: Burning coal, oil and gas for energy
options.rationale: Correct: burning fossil fuels releases carbon dioxide.
Correct: deforestation reduces carbon uptake and releases carbon.
Growing trees removes carbon dioxide rather than adding it.

options.text: Using electricity generated by wind turbines
options.rationale: Wind power adds little to no greenhouse gas during use.
